identity.quote: he likens the universe to the current of a river, saying that you cannot step twice into the same stream
identity.why: Plato, Cratylus 402a (Fowler tr.) is the classical attestation of the river saying; the cited English wording is a popular paraphrase with no single source of record.

evidence.quote: Heracleitus says, you know, that all things move and nothing remains still

title.value: \textit{{Y}ou cannot step twice into the same river; for other waters are continually flowing in}

notes: A quotation attribution, not a document. The exact cited wording was not found in a source of record; close variants: Burnet, Early Greek Philosophy (fr. 41-42): 'You cannot step twice into the same rivers; for fresh waters are ever flowing in upon you'; Plato Cratylus 402a: 'you cannot step twice into the same stream'; the fragment itself is DK 22 B12 (via Arius Didymus). '535 BCE' is a conventional birth-year estimate (c. 535 - c. 475 BCE), not a date of the saying. If a verifiable citation is wanted, cite a translation (e.g. Burnet 1920, or Plato's Cratylus) instead.
